newsitem.title: GREECE: Bank of America still bullish on the drachma.
newsitem.headline: Bank of America still bullish on the drachma.

text.p: Discouraging signs from the Greek fiscal front and wage overruns should not cast doubts on the sustainability of the hard drachma policy pursued by the central bank, said Bank of America in its bi-monthly market strategy report.

"Even though developments such as bad signs on the fiscal front and wage rate overruns could put pressure on the drachma, the sustainability of the hard drachma policy should not be brought into question," said Bank of America in its report on Italy Spain and Greece.

The central bank has said it wants to keep the drachma broadly stable against the currencies that make up the ecu to help attain its end-1997 inflation target of 4.5 percent and end-1998 goal of below 3.0 percent.
The drachma slid one percent versus the ecu in 1996 in line with Bank of Greece's target.

Ecu/drachma will fluctuate in the 303/307 band and mark/drachma in the 155/158 range in the next two months but ecu/drachma moves above the 306 level are good drachma buying, ecu selling opportunities, the report said.
"..and consider ecu/drachma rate hikes above the 306 level as good drachma buying opportunities," it said.

Bank of America recommended the long drachma, short ecu carry trade to investors with longer investment horizons and said high rate differentials favouring the drachma would continue to induce foreign currency inflows.
The hard drachma policy would be undeterred by a larger current account deficit estimated at $4.5 billion at the end of 1996, it said.

Bank of America said it expected market sentiment about Greek government securities to continue to be positive but predicted increased volatility ahead with taxable securities more sensitive to foreign capital flows. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
